text: _A high-ranking courtier with the ear of the local nobility._
motives: Curry favor, manufacture evidence, scheme

features.name: Devastating Retort
features.text: A PC who rolls less than 17 on an {{term:action-roll|action roll}} targeting the Advisor must mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}.

features.name: Bend Ears
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to influence an NPC within {{term:melee|Melee range}} with whispered words. That target’s opinion on one matter shifts toward the Advisor’s preference unless it is in direct opposition to the target’s motives.

features.name: Scapegoat
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to convince a crowd or notable individual that one person or group is responsible for some problem facing the target. The target becomes hostile to the scapegoat until convinced of their innocence with a successful {{term:presence|Presence}} Roll (17).

name: Rust Eater
text: _A pony-sized cockroach coated in a corrosive chitin that turns metal_ _into rust._
motives: Avoid detection, eat rust, sniff out metal

features.name: Stifling Pheromones
features.text: A PC who makes an {{term:action-roll|action roll}} within {{term:very-close|Very Close range}} of the Rust Eater must succeed on an {{term:instinct|Instinct}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}} or mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}.

features.name: Rust Touch
features.text: The Rust Eater’s carapace is coated in a corrosive acid that pits and rusts metal. When a PC within {{term:melee|Melee range}} of the Rust Easter succeeds on an attack against it with a metal weapon, reduce the weapon’s damage die by one step (for example, d8 to d6 or d6 to d4). If a weapon’s damage die is reduced below a d4, the weapon crumbles into rust. The Rust Eater then devours the rust pile and clears a {{term:hit-points|HP}}.

name: Secret-Keeper
text: _A clandestine leader with a direct channel to the Fallen Gods._
motives: Amass great power, plot, take command

features.name: Seize Your Moment
features.text: **Spend 2 {{term:fear|Fear}}** to {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} **1d4** allies. Attacks they make while spotlighted in this way deal half damage.

features.name: Our Master’s Will
features.text: When you {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} an ally within {{term:far|Far range}}, **mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to gain a {{term:fear|Fear}}.

features.name: Summoning Ritual
features.text: _Countdown (6)_. When the Secret-Keeper is in the {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} for the first time, activate the {{term:countdown|countdown}}. When they mark {{term:hit-points|HP}}, tick down this {{term:countdown|countdown}} by the number of {{term:hit-points|HP}} marked. When it triggers, summon a Minor Demon who appears at {{term:close|Close range}}.

features.name: Fallen Hounds
features.text: Once per scene, when the Secret-Keeper marks 2 or more {{term:hit-points|HP}}, you can **mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to summon a Demonic Hound Pack, which appears at {{term:close|Close range}} and is immediately spotlighted.

name: Scarecrow
text: _A bundle of straw bound into a humanoid shape, clothed in rags, and_ _animated by a trapped soul._
motives: Pull yourself together, scratch and claw

features.name: Made of Straw
features.text: The Scarecrow has {{term:resistance|resistance}} to physical damage but takes double damage from fire.

features.name: Terror Vision
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to have the Scarecrow lock eyes with a PC within {{term:very-close|Very Close range}}, dealing **2d8** magic damage and making them _{{term:vulnerable|Vulnerable}}_ until they roll with {{term:hope|Hope}}.

name: Shark
text: _A large aquatic predator, always on the move._
motives: Find the blood, isolate prey, target the weak

features.name: Terrifying
features.text: When the Shark makes a successful attack, all PCs within {{term:far|Far range}} lose a {{term:hope|Hope}} and you gain a {{term:fear|Fear}}.

features.name: Rending Bite
features.text: When the Shark makes a successful attack, the target must mark an {{term:armor-slot|Armor Slot}} without receiving its benefits (they can still use armor to reduce the damage). If they can’t mark an {{term:armor-slot|Armor Slot}}, they must mark an additional {{term:hit-points|HP}}.

features.name: Blood in the Water
features.text: When a creature within {{term:close|Close range}} of the Shark marks {{term:hit-points|HP}} from another creature’s attack, you can **mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to immediately {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} the Shark, moving them into {{term:melee|Melee range}} of the target and making a standard attack.

name: Siren
text: _A half-fish person with shimmering scales and an irresistible voice._
motives: Consume, lure prey, subdue with song

features.name: Captive Audience
features.text: If the Siren makes a standard attack against a target _Entranced_ by their song, the attack deals **2d10+1** damage instead of their standard damage.

features.name: Enchanting Song
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to sing a song that affects all targets within {{term:close|Close range}}. Targets must succeed on an {{term:instinct|Instinct}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}} or become _Entranced_ until they mark 2 {{term:stress|Stress}}. Other Sirens within {{term:close|Close range}} of the target can **mark** **a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to each add a +1 bonus to the {{term:difficulty|Difficulty}} of the {{term:reaction-roll|reaction roll}}. While _Entranced_, a target can’t act and is _{{term:vulnerable|Vulnerable}}_.

name: Sprite
text: _A tiny winged warrior that attacks trespassers with poison-tipped_ _arrows._
motives: Avoid detection, let the poison do its work, protect the wilderness

features.name: Minion (5)
features.text: The Sprite is defeated when they take any damage. For every 5 damage a PC deals to the Sprite, the PC defeats an additional Minion within range the attack would succeed against.

features.name: Art of Invisibility
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to make the Sprite _{{term:hidden|Hidden}}_ until they attack.

features.name: Dream Petal Poison
features.text: When the Sprite succeeds on a standard attack, you can **spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to make the target _Sleepy_ until the target takes damage. While _Sleepy_, the target must make a {{term:presence|Presence}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}} before they make an {{term:action-roll|action roll}}. On a failure, they must mark 2 {{term:stress|Stress}} or fall asleep until they take damage.

name: Spectral Archer
text: _A ghostly fighter with an ethereal bow, unable to move on while their_ _charge is vulnerable._
motives: Move through solid objects, stay out of the fray, rehash old battles

features.name: Ghost
features.text: The Archer has {{term:resistance|resistance}} to physical damage. **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to move up to {{term:close|Close range}} through solid objects.

features.name: Pick Your Target
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to make an attack within {{term:far|Far range}} against a PC who is within {{term:very-close|Very Close range}} of at least two other PCs. On a success, the target takes **2d8+12** physical damage.

name: Spectral Captain
text: _A ghostly commander leading their troops beyond death._
motives: Move through solid objects, rally troops, rehash old battles

features.name: Ghost
features.text: The Captain has {{term:resistance|resistance}} to physical damage. **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to move up to {{term:close|Close range}} through solid objects.

features.name: Unending Battle
features.text: **Spend 2 {{term:fear|Fear}}** to return up to **1d4+1** defeated Spectral allies to the battle at the points where they first appeared (with no marked {{term:hit-points|HP}} or {{term:stress|Stress}}).

features.name: Hold Fast
features.text: When the Captain’s Spectral allies are forced to make a {{term:reaction-roll|reaction roll}}, you can **mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to give those allies a +2 bonus to the roll.

features.name: Momentum
features.text: When the Captain makes a successful attack against a PC, you gain a {{term:fear|Fear}}.

name: Spectral Guardian
text: _A ghostly fighter with spears and swords, anchored by duty._
motives: Move through solid objects, protect treasure, rehash old battles

features.name: Ghost
features.text: The Guardian has {{term:resistance|resistance}} to physical damage. **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to move up to {{term:close|Close range}} through solid objects.

features.name: Grave Blade
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to make an attack against a target within {{term:very-close|Very Close range}}. On a success, deal **2d10+6** physical damage and the target must mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}.

name: Spy
text: _A skilled espionage agent with a knack for being in the right place to_ _overhear secrets._
motives: Cut and run, disguise appearance, eavesdrop

features.name: Gathering Secrets
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to describe how the Spy knows a secret about a PC in the scene.

features.name: Fly on the Wall
features.text: When a PC or group is discussing something sensitive, you can **mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to reveal that the Spy is present in the scene, observing them. If the Spy escapes the scene to report their findings, you gain **1d4** {{term:fear|Fear}}.

name: Stone Titan
text: _A gray-skinned goliath who lives underground and specializes in_ _crafting powerful items inlaid with magical runes._
motives: Blend into the rocks, craft and contemplate, pursue prophecy and solitude

features.name: Relentless (3)
features.text: The Titan can be spotlighted up to three times per GM turn. Spend {{term:fear|Fear}} as usual to {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} them.

features.name: Skillful Strike
features.text: Before the Titan makes an attack, you can **mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** and roll a **d6**. On a result of 3 or higher, the target’s {{term:evasion|Evasion}} is halved against this attack.

features.name: Sunlight Sickness
features.text: When the Titan first appears above ground, roll a **d4**. Mark a number of {{term:stress|Stress}} equal to the result. The Titan gains a bonus to their attack and damage rolls equal to the number of {{term:stress|Stress}} marked.

features.name: Hammer Smash
features.text: When a PC marks {{term:hit-points|HP}} from the Titan’s standard attack, you can **spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to force the target to mark an {{term:armor-slot|Armor Slot}} without gaining its benefits (they can still use armor to reduce the damage).

name: Stonewraith
text: _A prowling hunter, like a slinking mountain lion, with a slate-gray_ _stone body._
motives: Defend territory, isolate prey, stalk

features.name: Stonestrider
features.text: The Stonewraith can move through stone and earth as easily as air. While within stone or earth, they are _{{term:hidden|Hidden}}_ and {{term:immunity|immune}} to all damage.

features.name: Rocky Ambush
features.text: While _{{term:hidden|Hidden}}_, **mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to leap into {{term:melee|Melee range}} with a target within {{term:very-close|Very Close range}}. The target must succeed on an {{term:agility|Agility}} or {{term:instinct|Instinct}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}} (15) or take **2d8** physical damage and become {{term:temporary|temporarily}} _{{term:restrained|Restrained}}_.

features.name: Avalanche Roar
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to roar while within a cave and cause a cave-in. All targets within {{term:close|Close range}} must succeed on an {{term:agility|Agility}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}} (14) or take **2d10** physical damage. The rubble can be cleared with a Progress Countdown (8).

features.name: Momentum
features.text: When the Stonewraith makes a successful attack against a PC, you gain a {{term:fear|Fear}}.

name: Triceratops
text: _A large dinosaur that has an armored frill and three horns._
motives: Eat ferns, move in herds for protection, patrol the watering hole

features.name: Leathery Hide
features.text: When the Triceratops would be forced to mark {{term:hit-points|HP}}, you can **mark any number of {{term:stress|Stress}}** instead of an equal number of {{term:hit-points|HP}}.

features.name: Tail Swipe
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to choose up to three targets within {{term:very-close|Very Close range}}. Each target must make an {{term:agility|Agility}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}}. Targets who fail take **5d6** physical damage. Targets who succeed take half damage.

features.name: Bull Rush
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to choose a target within {{term:close|Close range}}. The Triceratops moves into {{term:melee|Melee range}} with the target and makes an attack. On a success, deal **3d10** direct physical damage.

name: Tyrannosaurus
text: _A huge carnivorous dinosaur that walks on two legs._
motives: Break through the treeline, eat, stomp around

features.name: Earth-Shaking Roar
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to force each PC within {{term:close|Close range}} to make a {{term:presence|Presence}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}}. On a failure, they must choose to lose a {{term:hope|Hope}} or mark **1d4** {{term:stress|Stress}}.

features.name: Stomp
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to attack a target within {{term:melee|Melee range}}. On a success, the target takes **3d12** direct physical damage.

features.name: Crushing Bite
features.text: When the Tyrannosaurus makes a successful standard attack, you can **spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to force the target to mark an additional {{term:hit-points|HP}}.

name: Urco
text: _A black-furred hound from beyond the veil of death that portends_ _death and feeds on fear._
motives: Feed, frighten, hunt

features.name: Fearmonger
features.text: When a PC within {{term:very-close|Very Close range}} fails with {{term:hope|Hope}}, you gain a {{term:fear|Fear}}.

features.name: Terror-Fueled
features.text: The Urco gains a bonus to attack and damage rolls equal to the number of {{term:fear|Fear}} you have.

features.name: Fear Eater
features.text: **Spend any number of {{term:fear|Fear}}** to clear the same number of {{term:stress|Stress}}. If the Urco has no marked {{term:stress|Stress}}, you can **spend any number of {{term:fear|Fear}}** to clear the same number of {{term:hit-points|HP}}.

features.name: Baleful Gaze
features.text: When the Urco takes damage from an attack, you can **spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to cause the attacker’s {{term:damage-thresholds|damage thresholds}} to gain a −1 penalty until the end of the scene. This effect can stack.

name: Valdenhax
text: _A malevolent forest hag who has long, mossy hair and flies through_ _the air with an oversized mortar and pestle._
motives: Collect souls, fly, vex trespassers

features.name: To Me, My Pretties
features.text: Once per scene, summon **2d4** Tier 2 Hordes, which appear at {{term:far|Far range}}. You gain a {{term:fear|Fear}} for each Horde summoned in this way.

features.name: Shadow Strangler
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to attack a target within {{term:far|Far range}}. On a success, the shadow of the Valdenhax’s hand stretches across the ground until it grasps the target’s shadow and drains their essence. The target marks **1d4** {{term:stress|Stress}}, and you gain an equal number of {{term:fear|Fear}}.

features.name: Corpse Whisperer
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to have the Valdenhax call out to the lingering spirit of a fallen ally within {{term:close|Close range}}. Roll a **d6**. On an even result, the Valdenhax resurrects the ally with half its {{term:hit-points|HP}} cleared. On an odd result, the Valdenhax absorbs the dregs of its life force and clears a {{term:stress|Stress}}.

features.name: Vexing Word
features.text: After a PC makes a roll, you can **mark a** **{{term:stress|Stress}}** to force them to reroll it. This feature can’t be used if the PC {{term:critical-success|critically succeeds}}.

name: War Wizard
text: _A battle-hardened mage trained in destructive magic._
motives: Develop new spells, seek power, shatter formations

features.name: Battle Teleport
features.text: Before or after making a standard attack, you can **mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to teleport to a location within {{term:far|Far range}}.

features.name: Refresh Warding Sphere
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to refresh the Wizard’s “Warding Sphere” reaction.

features.name: Eruption
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** and choose a point within {{term:far|Far range}}. A Very Close area around that point erupts into impassable terrain. All targets within that area must make an {{term:agility|Agility}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}} (14). Targets who fail take **2d10** physical damage and are thrown out of the area. Targets who succeed take half damage and aren’t moved.

features.name: Arcane Artillery
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to unleash a precise hail of magical blasts. All targets in the scene must make an {{term:agility|Agility}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}}. Targets who fail take **2d12** magic damage. Targets who succeed take half damage.

features.name: Warding Sphere
features.text: When the Wizard takes damage from an attack within {{term:close|Close range}}, deal **2d6** magic damage to the attacker. This reaction can’t be used again until the Wizard refreshes it with their “Refresh Warding Sphere” action.

name: Adult Flickerfly
text: _A winged insect the size of a large house with iridescent scales and_ _wings that move too fast to track._
motives: Collect shiny things, hunt, nest, swoop

features.name: Relentless (4)
features.text: The Flickerfly can be spotlighted up to four times per GM turn. Spend {{term:fear|Fear}} as usual to {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} them.

features.name: Never Misses
features.text: When the Flickerfly makes an attack, the target’s {{term:evasion|Evasion}} is halved against the attack.

features.name: Deadly Flight
features.text: While flying, the Flickerfly can move up to {{term:far|Far range}} instead of {{term:close|Close range}} before taking an action.

features.name: Whirlwind
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to whirl, making an attack against all targets within {{term:very-close|Very Close range}}. Targets the Flickerfly succeeds against take **3d8** direct physical damage.

features.name: Mind Dance
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to create a magically dazzling display that grapples the minds of nearby foes. All targets within {{term:close|Close range}} must make an {{term:instinct|Instinct}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}}. For each target who failed, you gain a {{term:fear|Fear}} and the Flickerfly learns one of the target’s fears.

features.name: Hallucinatory Breath
features.text: _Countdown (Loop 1d6)_. When the Flickerfly takes damage for the first time, activate the {{term:countdown|countdown}}. When it triggers, the Flickerfly breathes hallucinatory gas on all targets in front of them up to {{term:far|Far range}}. Targets must make an {{term:instinct|Instinct}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}} or be tormented by fearful hallucinations. Targets whose fears are known to the Flickerfly have {{term:disadvantage|disadvantage}} on this roll. Targets who fail lose 2 {{term:hope|Hope}} and take **3d8+3** direct magic damage.

features.name: Uncanny Reflexes
features.text: When the Flickerfly takes damage from an attack within {{term:close|Close range}}, you can **mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to take half damage.

name: Archmage
text: _A seeker of secret knowledge hidden away in a tome-filled tower._
motives: Corrupt, destroy, overwhelm with evil power

features.name: Relentless (3)
features.text: The Archmage can be spotlighted up to three times per GM turn. Spend {{term:fear|Fear}} as usual to {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} them.

features.name: Orbiting Aegis
features.text: When the Archmage appears, they conjure six discs of magical energy that orbit around them. Place a **d6** Aegis Die on this stat block with the 6 value facing up. When a PC makes a successful attack against the Archmage, roll a **d6**. If the result is equal to or less than the value of the Aegis Die, tick the Aegis Die down and ignore the damage. A PC can make a {{term:knowledge|Knowledge}} Roll to tick down the Aegis Die by 1 on a success or by 2 on a success with {{term:hope|Hope}}.

features.name: Force Salvo
features.text: **Spend any number of {{term:fear|Fear}}** and roll that many **d4s**. The Archmage unleashes a number of magical homing force bolts equal to the total result. For each bolt, a creature within {{term:far|Far range}} marks a {{term:hit-points|HP}}. The same creature can be targeted by up to three force bolts.

features.name: Fireball
features.text: **Mark any number of {{term:stress|Stress}}** to target the same number of PCs within {{term:far|Far range}}. Each target must succeed on an {{term:agility|Agility}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}} or take **4d10** magic damage.

features.name: Counterspell
features.text: When a PC succeeds on a {{term:spellcast-roll|Spellcast Roll}}, you can **spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to have the Archmage make a {{term:reaction-roll|reaction roll}} with a {{term:difficulty|Difficulty}} equal to the {{term:spellcast-roll|Spellcast Roll}}’s result. On a success, the PC’s {{term:spellcast-roll|Spellcast Roll}} fails instead, and you place a token on this stat block. Using this feature again costs additional {{term:fear|Fear}} equal to the number of tokens on this stat block. You can’t Counterspell a {{term:critical-success|critical success}}.

name: Catrin
text: _A lavishly adorned skeleton that has an endless appetite for gold._
motives: Dominate the conversation, seek attention, steal everything

features.name: Attracted to Wealth
features.text: PCs carrying at least a bag of gold gain {{term:advantage|advantage}} on {{term:presence|Presence}} Rolls made to influence the Catrin.

features.name: The Weight of Opulence
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to turn the Catrin’s gaze toward the PC carrying the most gold. The target must succeed on an {{term:instinct|Instinct}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}} or lose a {{term:hope|Hope}} for each bag of gold they’re carrying. If the PC loses their last {{term:hope|Hope}} or has no {{term:hope|Hope}} to lose, they mark {{term:stress|Stress}} instead.

features.name: Expensive Failure
features.text: When a PC within {{term:melee|Melee range}} fails an {{term:action-roll|action roll}}, you can **mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to have the Catrin brazenly steal a handful of gold from them.

name: Chimera
text: _A giant fire-breathing monster that has a lion’s head, a goat’s body,_ _and a serpent’s tail._
motives: Play with food, prowl territory, slay cattle

features.name: Rending Jaws
features.text: When the Chimera makes a successful attack against a PC, the target must mark 2 {{term:armor-slot|Armor Slots}} to reduce the severity by one threshold.

features.name: Double Claw
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to make two standard attacks. If both attacks succeed against the same target, combine the damage.

features.name: Breath of Fire
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to target up to three PCs in front of the Chimera within {{term:close|Close range}}. Each target must make an {{term:agility|Agility}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}} (20). Targets who fail take **3d12** magic damage. Targets who succeed must choose to mark either an {{term:armor-slot|Armor Slot}} or a {{term:stress|Stress}}.

features.name: Serpent Strike
features.text: When a PC within {{term:close|Close range}} targets the Chimera with an attack, you can **mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to attack the PC first. On a success, deal **4d4+10** physical damage and _Poison_ them until their next rest or they succeed on a {{term:knowledge|Knowledge}} Roll (20). While _Poisoned,_ the target must roll a **d6** before they make an {{term:action-roll|action roll}}. On a result of 3 or lower, they must mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}.

name: Crimson Lepus
text: _A red-eyed rabbit that thinks only of murder._
motives: Be cute, go for the throat, hop around

features.name: Relentless (3)
features.text: The Lepus can be spotlighted up to three times per GM turn. Spend {{term:fear|Fear}} as usual to {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} it.

features.name: “Awww...”
features.text: When the Lepus first appears, it is _Too Cute_. To attack a _Too Cute_ creature, a PC must succeed on an {{term:instinct|Instinct}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}} (20). Clear the _Too Cute_ condition if a PC deals damage to the Lepus or if the Lepus attacks a PC.

features.name: Terrifying
features.text: When the Lepus makes a successful attack, all PCs within {{term:close|Close range}} lose a {{term:hope|Hope}}, and you gain a {{term:fear|Fear}}.

features.name: Leaping Jugular Strike
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to have the Lepus leap into {{term:melee|Melee range}} of a target within {{term:far|Far range}} and make an attack against them. On a success, deal **3d20** direct physical damage. If the target marks {{term:hit-points|HP}} from this attack, they become _{{term:vulnerable|Vulnerable}}_ until they clear a {{term:hit-points|HP}}.

features.name: Evasive
features.text: When the Lepus would take damage, roll a **d6**. On a 4 or higher, halve the damage. If the damage was already halved, the Lepus takes no damage.

features.name: “Run Away!”
features.text: When a PC with no {{term:hope|Hope}} takes the {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} within {{term:very-far|Very Far range}} of the Lepus, the PC must succeed on a {{term:presence|Presence}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}} or use their action to flee the battlefield until they spend a {{term:hope|Hope}} to return.

name: Cryptimoth
text: _A large red-eyed moth creature that walks upright and portends_ _mysterious or evil events._
motives: Echolocate, fly silently, melt into the shadows

features.name: Terrifying
features.text: When the Cryptimoth makes a successful attack, all PCs within {{term:close|Close range}} lose a {{term:hope|Hope}}, and you gain a {{term:fear|Fear}}.

features.name: Psychic Screech
features.text: **Spend 2 {{term:fear|Fear}}** to have the Cryptimoth unleash a burst of psychic energy that causes each PC within {{term:far|Far range}} to suffer visions of their horrifying fate. Each target must make an {{term:instinct|Instinct}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}} (16). Targets who fail take **3d8** direct magic damage and become _{{term:vulnerable|Vulnerable}}_ until their next rest. Targets who succeed must mark a {{term:stress|Stress}} or take half damage.

features.name: Shadow Swarm
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to have the Cryptimoth conjure a swarm of mothlike shadow creatures within {{term:far|Far range}}. The swarm fills a {{term:close|Close range}} area and blocks line of sight. Creatures that aren’t Cryptimoths are _{{term:vulnerable|Vulnerable}}_ while inside that area and must mark a {{term:stress|Stress}} to move through it. A PC can dispel the swarm with a successful {{term:spellcast-roll|Spellcast Roll}} (12).

features.name: Paranoia Glare
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to have the Cryptimoth gaze into the eyes of a PC within {{term:close|Close range}} and make them _Paranoid_. While _Paranoid_, the PC is suspicious of other PCs and can’t {{term:help-an-ally|Help an Ally}} or take part in {{term:tag-team-roll|Tag Team Rolls}}. To clear this condition, the PC must succeed on an {{term:instinct|Instinct}} Roll (16) or participate in the Prepare {{term:downtime|downtime move}} with one or more members of their party during a rest.

name: Cursed Merfolk
text: _A half-fish, half-human creature psychically bound to serve the Deep_ _Dwellers._
motives: Separate enemies, strike from the shadows, use aquatic environment to advantage

features.name: Fish-Tailed
features.text: The Merfolk is _{{term:vulnerable|Vulnerable}}_ out of the water.

features.name: Gang Up
features.text: The Merfolk gains a +2 bonus to attack rolls against targets within {{term:melee|Melee range}} of one or more allies.

features.name: “Get Over Here!”
features.text: When the Merfolk makes a successful standard attack against a target beyond {{term:melee|Melee range}}, you can **mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to pull them into {{term:melee|Melee range}}. If you do, you can **spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to make a standard attack with {{term:advantage|advantage}} against the target.

name: Deep Dweller
text: _A huge psychic lamprey that has pitch-black eyes and toxic tentacles._
motives: Abuse power, seek worship, stalk sunken ruins

features.name: Psychic Blast
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to choose up to three targets within {{term:close|Close range}} and force them to make an {{term:instinct|Instinct}} or {{term:knowledge|Knowledge}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}}. Targets who succeed mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}. Targets who fail take **3d10+4** direct magic damage and are _{{term:vulnerable|Vulnerable}}_ until spotlighted.

features.name: Brain Drain
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to choose a _{{term:vulnerable|Vulnerable}}_ PC within {{term:very-close|Very Close range}}. The target marks **1d4** {{term:stress|Stress}}, and the Deep Dweller clears an equal number of {{term:hit-points|HP}}.

features.name: Call of the Deep
features.text: **Spend 2 {{term:fear|Fear}}** to summon **1d4** Cursed Merfolk, who appear at {{term:far|Far range}} and immediately take the {{term:spotlight|spotlight}}.

features.name: Mucosal Contamination
features.text: Make an attack roll against a PC within {{term:very-close|Very Close range}}. On a success, the Deep Dweller uses its tentacles to immobilize the target, sliming them with toxic sludge. The target is _{{term:restrained|Restrained}}_ until they break free or slip out with a successful {{term:strength|Strength}} or {{term:finesse|Finesse}} Roll. Each time the Deep Dweller is spotlighted, all PCs _{{term:restrained|Restrained}}_ in this way take **3d8** direct physical damage. The Deep Dweller releases all creatures _{{term:restrained|Restrained}}_ by it when it’s defeated or takes {{term:damage-thresholds|Severe damage}}.

name: Demon of Avarice
text: _A regal cloaked monstrosity with circular horns adorned_ _with treasure._
motives: Consume, fuel greed, sow dissent

features.name: Money Talks
features.text: Attacks against the Demon are made with {{term:disadvantage|disadvantage}} unless the attacker spends a handful of gold. This Demon starts with a number of handfuls equal to the number of PCs. When a target marks {{term:hit-points|HP}} from the Demon’s standard attack, they can spend a handful of gold instead of marking {{term:hit-points|HP}} (1 handful per {{term:hit-points|HP}}). Add a handful of gold to the Demon for each handful of gold spent by PCs on this feature.

features.name: Numbers Must Go Up
features.text: Add a bonus to the Demon’s attack rolls equal to the number of handfuls of gold they have.

features.name: Money Is Time
features.text: **Spend 3 handfuls of gold (or a {{term:fear|Fear}})** to {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} **1d4+1** allies.

name: Demon of Despair
text: _A cloaked demon-creature with long limbs, seeping shadows._
motives: Make fear contagious, stick to the shadows, undermine resolve

features.name: Depths of Despair
features.text: The Demon deals double damage to PCs with 0 {{term:hope|Hope}}.

features.name: Your Struggle Is Pointless
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to weigh down the spirits of all PCs within {{term:far|Far range}}. All targets affected replace their {{term:duality-dice|Hope Die}} with a **d8** until they roll a success with {{term:hope|Hope}} or their next rest.

features.name: Your Friends Will Fail You
features.text: When a PC fails with {{term:fear|Fear}}, you can **mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to cause all other PCs within {{term:close|Close range}} to lose a {{term:hope|Hope}}.

features.name: Momentum
features.text: When the Demon makes a successful attack against a PC, you gain a {{term:fear|Fear}}.

name: Demon of Hubris
text: _A perfectly beautiful and infinitely cruel demon with a gleaming_ _spear and elegant robes._
motives: Condescend, declare premature victory, prove superiority

features.name: Terrifying
features.text: When the Demon makes a successful attack, all PCs within {{term:far|Far range}} must lose a {{term:hope|Hope}} and you gain a {{term:fear|Fear}}.

features.name: Double or Nothing
features.text: When a PC within {{term:far|Far range}} fails a roll, they can choose to reroll their {{term:duality-dice|Fear Die}} and take the new result. If they still fail, they mark 2 {{term:stress|Stress}} and the Demon clears a {{term:stress|Stress}}.

features.name: Unparalleled Skill
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to deal the Demon’s standard attack damage to a target within {{term:close|Close range}}.

features.name: The Root of Villainy
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} two other Demons within {{term:far|Far range}}.

features.name: You Pale in Comparison
features.text: When a PC fails a roll within {{term:close|Close range}} of the Demon, they must mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}.

name: Demon of Jealousy
text: _A fickle creature of spindly limbs and insatiable desires._
motives: Join in on others’ success, take what belongs to others, hold grudges

features.name: Unprotected Mind
features.text: The Demon’s standard attack deals {{term:direct-damage|direct damage}}.

features.name: My Turn
features.text: When the Demon marks {{term:hit-points|HP}} from an attack, **spend a number of {{term:fear|Fear}} equal to the {{term:hit-points|HP}} marked by the Demon** to cause the attacker to mark the same number of {{term:hit-points|HP}}.

features.name: Rivalry
features.text: When a creature within {{term:close|Close range}} takes damage from a different adversary, you can **mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to add a **d4** to the damage roll.

features.name: What’s Yours Is Mine
features.text: When a PC takes {{term:damage-thresholds|Severe damage}} within {{term:very-close|Very Close range}} of the Demon, you can **spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to cause the target to make a {{term:finesse|Finesse}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}}. On a failure, the Demon seizes one item or consumable of their choice from the target’s inventory.

name: Demon of Wrath
text: _A hulking demon with boulder-sized fists, driven by endless rage._
motives: Fuel anger, impress rivals, wreak havoc

features.name: Anger Unrelenting
features.text: The Demon’s attacks deal {{term:direct-damage|direct damage}}.

features.name: Battle Lust
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to boil the blood of all PCs within {{term:far|Far range}}. They use a d20 as their {{term:duality-dice|Fear Die}} until the end of the scene.

features.name: Retaliation
features.text: When the Demon takes damage from an attack within {{term:close|Close range}}, you can **mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to make a standard attack against the attacker.

features.name: Blood and Souls
features.text: _Countdown (Loop 6)_. Activate the first time an attack is made within sight of the Demon. It ticks down when a PC takes a violent action. When it triggers, summon **1d4** Minor Demons, who appear at {{term:close|Close range}}.

name: Drake
text: _A clawed quadruped that has a scaled, serpentine body and a_ _willingness to serve its cousins, the dragons._
motives: Coil and crush, protect master, slither around lairs and ruins, strike first

features.name: Relentless (2)
features.text: The Drake can be spotlighted up to two times per GM turn. Spend {{term:fear|Fear}} as usual to {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} it.

features.name: Guard Dog
features.text: When a PC would deal damage to a creature within {{term:close|Close range}}, you can **mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to have the Drake move to intercept the attack and take the damage instead. If the attacker is within {{term:melee|Melee range}} of the Drake’s new position, you can immediately {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} the Drake without spending {{term:fear|Fear}}.

name: Dire Bat
text: _A wide-winged pet endlessly loyal to their vampire owner._
motives: Dive-bomb, hide, protect leader

features.name: Flying
features.text: While flying, the Bat gains a +3 bonus to their {{term:difficulty|Difficulty}}.

features.name: Screech
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to send a high-pitch screech out toward all targets in front of the Bat within {{term:far|Far range}}. Those targets must mark **1d4** {{term:stress|Stress}}.

features.name: Guardian
features.text: When an allied Vampire marks {{term:hit-points|HP}}, you can **mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to fly into {{term:melee|Melee range}} of the attacker and make an attack with {{term:advantage|advantage}} against them. On a success, deal **2d6+2** physical damage.

name: Dryad
text: _A nature spirit in the form of a humanoid tree._
motives: Command, cultivate, drive out, preserve the forest

features.name: Bramble Patch
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to target a point within {{term:far|Far range}}. Create a patch of thorns that covers an area within {{term:close|Close range}} of that point. All targets within that area take **2d6+2** physical damage when they act. A target must succeed on a {{term:finesse|Finesse}} Roll or deal more than 20 damage to the Dryad with an attack to leave the area.

features.name: Grow Saplings
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to grow three Treant Sapling Minions, who appear at {{term:close|Close range}} and immediately take the {{term:spotlight|spotlight}}.

features.name: We Are All One
features.text: When an ally dies within {{term:close|Close range}}, you can **spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to clear 2 {{term:hit-points|HP}} and 2 {{term:stress|Stress}} as the fallen ally’s life force is returned to the forest.

name: Dullahan
text: _A horse-mounted specter holding their own severed head in one hand_ _and wielding a whip fashioned from a human spine in the other._
motives: Doom with a glance, gallop across water, kick with heavy hooves

features.name: Specter
features.text: The Dullahan has {{term:resistance|resistance}} to physical damage. **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to move up to {{term:close|Close range}} through solid objects.

features.name: Spectral Mount
features.text: While atop their steed, the Dullahan can move up to {{term:far|Far range}} instead of {{term:close|Close range}} before taking an action. If the Dullahan is unhorsed, their mount disappears until you **mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to summon it again. The Dullahan is _{{term:vulnerable|Vulnerable}}_ while not on their horse.

features.name: Bone Whip Strike
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to make an attack against a target within {{term:melee|Melee range}}. On a success, the target takes **4d4+10** direct physical damage and is _{{term:vulnerable|Vulnerable}}_ until they clear a {{term:hit-points|HP}}.

features.name: Death Glare
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to choose a PC within {{term:far|Far range}}. The target must make an {{term:presence|Presence}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}} (19). On a success, they mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}. On a failure, they mark a {{term:hit-points|HP}} and activate a Doom Countdown (4). It ticks down when the Dullahan is spotlighted. When it triggers, the target makes a {{term:death-move|death move}}. If the Dullahan is defeated or the PCs take a rest, all Doom Countdowns end.

name: Elemental Spark
text: _A blazing mote of elemental fire._
motives: Blast, consume, gain mass

features.name: Minion (9)
features.text: The Elemental is defeated when they take any damage. For every 9 damage a PC deals to the Elemental, defeat an additional Minion within range the attack would succeed against.

features.name: Group Attack
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to choose a target and {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} all Elemental Sparks within {{term:close|Close range}} of them. Those Minions move into {{term:melee|Melee range}} of the target and make one shared attack roll. On a success, they deal 5 physical damage each. Combine this damage.

name: Fellmounted Shadow King
text: _The shade of a forgotten ruler, cursed to patrol the skies atop a_ _winged eel in the service of an even greater evil._
motives: Find magic items, inspire fear, patrol skies

features.name: Fellmount
features.text: While the Shadow King is on his mount, he gains a +2 bonus to his {{term:difficulty|Difficulty}}. When the Shadow King takes {{term:damage-thresholds|Severe damage}}, he’s knocked from his mount. If the Shadow King is unmounted, his mount disappears until you **mark a** **{{term:stress|Stress}}** to summon it again.

features.name: Light and Shadow
features.text: The Shadow King has {{term:advantage|advantage}} on attack rolls while in shadow or darkness and {{term:disadvantage|disadvantage}} on attack rolls while in bright light.

features.name: Relic Hunter
features.text: The Shadow King has {{term:advantage|advantage}} on attack rolls against PCs who have magic weapons or armor equipped.

features.name: Hellsong
features.text: **Spend 2 {{term:fear|Fear}}** to have the Shadow King’s mount unleash a spine-chilling screech that echoes over the battlefield. Each PC within {{term:far|Far range}} must make a {{term:presence|Presence}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}} (18). Targets who succeed must mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}. Targets who fail must mark a {{term:stress|Stress}} and lose a {{term:hope|Hope}}. If a PC can’t lose a {{term:hope|Hope}}, you gain 2 {{term:fear|Fear}}.

features.name: Air Support
features.text: Three times per scene, you can **spend a** **{{term:fear|Fear}}** to have an ally within {{term:far|Far range}} reroll a failed attack with {{term:advantage|advantage}}.

name: Fire Titan
text: _An armor-clad goliath who has ash-gray skin and fiery hair and_ _wields a masterwork greatsword crafted in their own smithy._
motives: Act valorously, make war, think tactically

features.name: Relentless (3)
features.text: The Titan can be spotlighted up to three times per GM turn. Spend {{term:fear|Fear}} as usual to {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} them.

features.name: Masterwork Armor
features.text: _Countdown (3)._ When the Titan first appears, activate the {{term:countdown|countdown}}. It ticks down when the Titan takes Major or {{term:damage-thresholds|Severe damage}}. Until the {{term:countdown|countdown}} triggers, reduce {{term:incoming-damage|incoming damage}} by **1d12**. When it triggers, the Titan gains a +1 bonus to their {{term:difficulty|Difficulty}} and attack rolls.

features.name: Momentum
features.text: When the Titan makes a successful attack against a PC, you gain a {{term:fear|Fear}}.

features.name: Hurl Rock
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to choose a point within {{term:far|Far range}}, then make an attack against all targets between the Titan and that point. Targets the Titan succeeds against take **3d12** physical damage.

features.name: Skull Splitter
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to place a token on this stat block. The next time the Titan is spotlighted, you must **spend** **the token** from this stat block and make an attack against a PC within {{term:close|Close range}}. On a success, deal **3d20+5** direct physical damage. On a failure, the target marks a {{term:stress|Stress}}.

features.name: Blazing Heart
features.text: When the Titan marks half or more of their {{term:hit-points|HP}}, you can **spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** and **mark any number of {{term:stress|Stress}}** to clear a number of {{term:hit-points|HP}} equal to the number of {{term:stress|Stress}} marked.

name: Frost Titan
text: _A blue-skinned goliath who has rimed hair and wears trophies of past_ _battles._
motives: Claim trophies, raid and pillage, test mettle

features.name: Relentless (2)
features.text: The Titan can be spotlighted up to two times per GM turn. Spend {{term:fear|Fear}} as usual to {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} them.

features.name: War Horn
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to force each PC within {{term:far|Far range}} to succeed on a {{term:presence|Presence}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}} or mark a {{term:stress|Stress}} and become _{{term:vulnerable|Vulnerable}}_ until after the next attack against them.

features.name: Bull Rush
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to move up to {{term:close|Close range}} and make an attack roll against a target within {{term:melee|Melee range}}. On a success, deal **4d10+2** physical damage and knock the target back to {{term:close|Close range}}.

features.name: Cleaving Strike
features.text: When a PC marks {{term:hit-points|HP}} from the Titan’s standard attack, you can **mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to force another PC within {{term:very-close|Very Close range}} who the attack would have succeeded against to mark the same number of {{term:hit-points|HP}}.

features.name: Trophy Hunter
features.text: When the Titan defeats a PC, the Titan takes the PC’s most valuable possession as a trophy.

name: Gargantuan Sea Turtle
text: _A monstrous sea turtle that has an adamantine shell and beak._
motives: Acquire riches, capsize trading vessels, lie in wait, use the waves as cover

features.name: Relentless (3)
features.text: The Turtle can be spotlighted up to three times per GM turn. Spend {{term:fear|Fear}} as usual to {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} it.

features.name: Piercing Bite
features.text: When the Turtle makes a successful standard attack against a PC, the PC must either mark an {{term:armor-slot|Armor Slot}} without receiving its benefit or take double damage.

features.name: Tail Bash
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to make a standard attack against all PCs behind the Turtle within {{term:very-close|Very Close range}}. On a success, a target takes an extra **1d12** physical damage and is pushed away from the Turtle to {{term:close|Close range}}.

features.name: Gigaton Splash
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to have the Turtle use its weight to unleash an unstoppable wall of water that targets all creatures within {{term:far|Far range}}. Each PC must make a {{term:strength|Strength}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}} to navigate the tide. Targets who fail are pushed away from the Turtle to {{term:close|Close range}}, take **4d8** physical damage, and become {{term:temporary|temporarily}} _{{term:vulnerable|Vulnerable}}_. Targets who succeed must mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}. For each target who failed, you gain a {{term:fear|Fear}}.

features.name: Steam Breath
features.text: **Spend 2 {{term:fear|Fear}}** to have the Turtle release a blast of superheated steam targeting all PCs in front of it within {{term:close|Close range}}. Each target must make an {{term:agility|Agility}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}}. Targets who fail take **4d8** magic damage and become {{term:temporary|temporarily}} _{{term:vulnerable|Vulnerable}}._ Targets who succeed must choose to either mark a {{term:stress|Stress}} or take half damage.

name: Greater Earth Elemental
text: _A living landslide of boulders and dust, as large as a house._
motives: Avalanche, knock over, pummel

features.name: Slow
features.text: When you {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} the Elemental and they don’t have a token on their stat block, they can’t act yet. Place a token on their stat block and describe what they’re preparing to do. When you {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} the Elemental and they have a token on their stat block, clear the token and they can act.

features.name: Crushing Blows
features.text: When the Elemental makes a successful attack, the target must mark an {{term:armor-slot|Armor Slot}} without receiving its benefits (they can still use armor to reduce the damage). If they can’t mark an {{term:armor-slot|Armor Slot}}, they must mark an additional {{term:hit-points|HP}}.

features.name: Immovable Object
features.text: An attack that would move the Elemental moves them two fewer ranges (for example, Far becomes Very Close). When the Elemental takes physical damage, reduce it by 7.

features.name: Rockslide
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to create a rockslide that buries the land in front of Elemental within {{term:close|Close range}} with rockfall. All targets in this area must make an {{term:agility|Agility}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}} (19). Targets who fail take **2d12+5** physical damage and become _{{term:vulnerable|Vulnerable}}_ until their next roll with {{term:hope|Hope}}. Targets who succeed take half damage.

features.name: Momentum
features.text: When the Elemental makes a successful attack against a PC, you gain a {{term:fear|Fear}}.

name: Greater Water Elemental
text: _A huge living wave that crashes down upon enemies._
motives: Deluge, disperse, drown

features.name: Water Jet
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to attack a target within {{term:very-close|Very Close range}}. On a success, deal **2d4+7** physical damage and the target’s next action has {{term:disadvantage|disadvantage}}. On a failure, the target must mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}.

features.name: Drowning Embrace
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to make an attack against all targets within {{term:very-close|Very Close range}}. Targets the Elemental succeeds against become _{{term:restrained|Restrained}}_ and _{{term:vulnerable|Vulnerable}}_ as they begin drowning. A target can break free, ending both conditions, with a successful {{term:strength|Strength}} or {{term:instinct|Instinct}} Roll.

features.name: High Tide
features.text: When the Elemental makes a successful standard attack, you can **mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to knock the target back to {{term:close|Close range}}.

name: Huge Green Ooze
text: _A translucent green mound of acid taller than most humans._
motives: Camouflage, creep up, envelop, multiply

features.name: Slow
features.text: When you {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} the Ooze and they don’t have a token on their stat block, they can’t act yet. Place a token on their stat block and describe what they’re preparing to do. When you {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} the Ooze and they have a token on their stat block, clear the token and they can act.

features.name: Acidic Form
features.text: When the Ooze makes a successful attack, the target must mark an {{term:armor-slot|Armor Slot}} without receiving its benefits (they can still use armor to reduce the damage). If they can’t mark an {{term:armor-slot|Armor Slot}}, they must mark an additional {{term:hit-points|HP}}.

features.name: Envelop
features.text: Make an attack against a target within {{term:melee|Melee range}}. On a success, the Ooze _Envelops_ them and the target must mark 2 {{term:stress|Stress}}. While _Enveloped_, the target must mark an additional {{term:stress|Stress}} every time they make an {{term:action-roll|action roll}}. When the Ooze takes {{term:damage-thresholds|Severe damage}}, all _Enveloped_ targets are freed and the condition is cleared.

features.name: Split
features.text: When the Ooze has 4 or more {{term:hit-points|HP}} marked, you can **spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to split them into two Green Oozes (with no marked {{term:hit-points|HP}} or {{term:stress|Stress}}). Immediately {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} both of them.

name: Hydra
text: _A quadrupedal scaled beast with multiple long-necked heads, each_ _filled with menacing fangs._
motives: Devour, regenerate, terrify

features.name: Many-Headed Menace
features.text: The Hydra begins with three heads and can have up to five. When the Hydra takes Major or greater damage, they lose a head.

features.name: Relentless (X)
features.text: The Hydra can be spotlighted X times per GM turn, where X is the Hydra’s number of heads. Spend {{term:fear|Fear}} as usual to {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} them.

features.name: Regeneration
features.text: If the Hydra has any marked {{term:hit-points|HP}}, **spend a** **{{term:fear|Fear}}** to clear a {{term:hit-points|HP}} and grow two heads.

features.name: Terrifying Chorus
features.text: All PCs within {{term:far|Far range}} lose 2 {{term:hope|Hope}}.

features.name: Magical Weakness
features.text: When the Hydra takes magic damage, they become _Dazed_ until the next roll with {{term:fear|Fear}}. While _Dazed_, they can’t use their Regeneration action but are {{term:immunity|immune}} to magic damage.

name: Lamia
text: _A snake-tailed humanoid monster who stalks the night to absorb the_ _life energy of sleeping people._
motives: Attack the unaware, avoid sunlight, leech life force, put to sleep, slither through tall grass

features.name: Constriction
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to have the Lamia wrap their tail around a PC within {{term:melee|Melee range}} and squeeze. The target must succeed on a {{term:finesse|Finesse}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}} or become _Constricted_ until the Lamia moves or takes Major or greater damage. While _Constricted_, the target is _{{term:restrained|Restrained}}_ and must mark a {{term:stress|Stress}} when the Lamia takes the {{term:spotlight|spotlight}}.

features.name: Life Leech
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to force a _{{term:vulnerable|Vulnerable}}_ or _{{term:restrained|Restrained}}_ target within {{term:melee|Melee range}} to mark **1d4−1** {{term:hit-points|HP}}. The Lamia then clears an equal number of {{term:hit-points|HP}}.

features.name: Sleep Toxin
features.text: When the Lamia makes a successful standard attack against a PC, you can **spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to make them _{{term:vulnerable|Vulnerable}}_ until they succeed on a {{term:instinct|Instinct}} Roll (19).

name: Lamplight Beguiler
text: _A huge aquatic creature that lures unwary prey into eating range_ _with its dangling, shapeshifting head stalk._
motives: Entice with secret knowledge, snap the trap shut, speak through a shapeshifted head stalk

features.name: Doppel-Dangler
features.text: The membranous cluster at the end of the Beguiler’s head stalk can shapeshift into any humanoid form. **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to choose a PC within {{term:close|Close range}}. Their player must tell you who their PC would find most trustworthy. The Beguiler’s head stalk transforms into that person and gains the ability to speak in their voice.

features.name: Entice
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to have the Beguiler make an alluring overture to a PC within {{term:close|Close range}}. The PC must succeed on a {{term:presence|Presence}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}} (18) or move into {{term:melee|Melee range}} with the Beguiler. If the Beguiler’s head stalk is transformed into a person the PC would find trustworthy, they have {{term:disadvantage|disadvantage}} on the {{term:reaction-roll|reaction roll}}.

features.name: Gulp
features.text: When a PC moves within {{term:melee|Melee range}}, you can **spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to make an attack roll against them. On a successful attack, the target takes **3d6** physical damage and is _Swallowed_. While _Swallowed_, the target is _{{term:restrained|Restrained}}_ and takes **3d6** physical damage when the Beguiler takes the {{term:spotlight|spotlight}}. The Beguiler disgorges all _Swallowed_ creatures when it takes Major or {{term:damage-thresholds|Severe damage}}.

name: Manticore
text: _A legendary beast that has a human’s face, lion’s body, scorpion’s_ _tail, and dragon’s wings._
motives: Bite, claw, pounce, riddle, swipe, swoop, trick

features.name: Relentless (3)
features.text: The Manticore can be spotlighted up to three times per GM turn. Spend {{term:fear|Fear}} as usual to {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} them.

features.name: Riddle Me This
features.text: The Manticore is obsessed with puzzles and can be distracted by brain teasers, word games, or other semi-intellectual diversions.

features.name: Winged
features.text: While airborne, the Manticore gains a +2 bonus to their {{term:difficulty|Difficulty}} and attack rolls.

features.name: Pouncing Attack
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to have the Manticore pounce into {{term:melee|Melee range}} of a target within {{term:far|Far range}} and make an attack against them. On a success, deal **3d20+6** physical damage, and the target becomes _Shaky_ until they spend a {{term:hope|Hope}}. While _Shaky_, the target makes attack rolls with {{term:disadvantage|disadvantage}}.

features.name: Paralyzing Tail Spike
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to make an attack roll against a target within {{term:close|Close range}}. On a success, the target takes **3d8** physical damage and becomes _{{term:restrained|Restrained}}_ until they overcome the toxin with a successful {{term:strength|Strength}} Roll.

features.name: Locking Jaws
features.text: When the Manticore succeeds on a standard attack against a target within {{term:melee|Melee range}}, you can **mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to lock their jaws onto the target, making the target _{{term:restrained|Restrained}}_ and _{{term:vulnerable|Vulnerable}}_ until they escape with a successful {{term:strength|Strength}} Roll (19).

name: Monarch
text: _The sovereign ruler of a nation, wreathed in the privilege of tradition_ _and wielding unmatched power in their domain._
motives: Control vassals, destroy rivals, forge a legacy

features.name: Execute Them!
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** per PC in the party to have the group condemned for crimes real or imagined. A PC who succeeds on a {{term:presence|Presence}} Roll can demand trial by combat or another special form of trial.

features.name: Crownsguard
features.text: Once per scene, **mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to summon six Tier 3 Minions, who appear at {{term:close|Close range}} to enforce the Monarch’s will.

features.name: Casus Belli
features.text: _Long-Term Countdown (8)_. **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to activate after the Monarch’s desire for war is first revealed. When it triggers, the Monarch has a reason to rally the nation to war and the support to act on that reason. You gain **1d4** {{term:fear|Fear}}.

name: Night Children
text: _A teeming assortment of nocturnal fiends under the thrall of an_ _ancient evil._
motives: Carry victims back to master, overrun settlements, slither through shadow

features.name: Horde (2d6+2)
features.text: When the Night Children have marked half or more of their {{term:hit-points|HP}}, their standard attack deals **2d6+2** physical damage instead.

features.name: Swell Ranks
features.text: Once per scene, **mark any number of {{term:stress|Stress}}** to have the Night Children open a portal that spews forth reinforcements, refilling the Horde’s ranks. Clear a number of {{term:hit-points|HP}} equal to the number of {{term:stress|Stress}} marked.

features.name: Overwhelm
features.text: When the Night Children mark {{term:hit-points|HP}} from an attack within {{term:melee|Melee range}}, you can **mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to make a standard attack against the attacker.

name: Pain Priest
text: _A member of an other-dimensional religious order devoted to_ _exploring the boundaries of mortal suffering and ecstasy._
motives: Feed on emotions, locate the innocent or curious, tempt them with their deepest desires

features.name: Walk Between Worlds
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to place the Priest anywhere within {{term:very-far|Very Far range}} and immediately {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} them again.

features.name: Pleasure and Pain
features.text: When a PC within {{term:close|Close range}} of the Priest gains a {{term:hope|Hope}} or marks {{term:hit-points|HP}}, roll a **d8**. On a result of 8, the Priest opens a portal to their original dimension and flees there with the closest party member. You gain **1d6** {{term:fear|Fear}}. The portal remains open until the Priest is defeated or spotlighted again.

name: Phoenix
text: _A huge eagle that’s made of magical flame, impossible to kill, and_ _hunted for its healing plumage._
motives: Flee pursuers, live brilliantly, soar through the heavens, wield light and flame

features.name: Purifying Aura
features.text: Any PC who takes an action within the Phoenix’s {{term:melee|Melee range}} can spend a {{term:hope|Hope}} to purify themself in its healing warmth, clearing a {{term:hit-points|HP}} or a {{term:stress|Stress}} and all conditions.

features.name: Fireseed
features.text: The Phoenix bleeds magic fire. When the Phoenix marks a {{term:hit-points|HP}}, summon one Minor Fire Elemental within {{term:very-close|Very Close range}}.

features.name: Resurrection
features.text: When the Phoenix is defeated, it becomes a cloud of ash that blows away to reveal a Smoldering Egg. The Egg is {{term:immunity|immune}} to all damage and has a heat aura that deals **3d4** direct magic damage to anyone who touches it. The Egg hatches into a new Phoenix, with all {{term:hit-points|HP}} and {{term:stress|Stress}} cleared, in 7 days.

name: Plesiosaurus
text: _A canoe-length marine lizard that has a long neck and four flippers._
motives: Dive deeper, eat fish, swim peacefully

features.name: Only a Rumor
features.text: While deep underwater, the Plesiosaurus can’t be located or targeted.

features.name: Wall of Water
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to have the Plesiosaurus breach and crash, sending a wall of water from one side of its body. Each PC within {{term:far|Far range}} on that side of the Plesiosaurus must succeed on an {{term:agility|Agility}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}} (18) or take **3d10** physical damage and be pushed back to {{term:far|Far range}}.

name: Roc
text: _A giant falcon that nests in the mountains and unleashes storms._
motives: Breathe lightning and speak thunder, protect eggs, rake with talons, spy from afar

features.name: Relentless (3)
features.text: The Roc can be spotlighted up to three times per GM turn. Spend {{term:fear|Fear}} as usual to {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} it.

features.name: Bird of Prey
features.text: Once per GM turn, the Roc can move up to {{term:very-far|Very Far range}} before or after it takes an action.

features.name: Here Comes the Boom
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to have the Roc unleash a storm of lightning and thunder. Make an attack roll against **1d4+1** targets within {{term:far|Far range}}. Targets the Roc succeeds against take **3d12** magic damage. Then each target within {{term:far|Far range}} of the Roc must make an {{term:agility|Agility}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}} (20). Targets who fail take **3d8** physical damage and are pushed back to {{term:close|Close range}}. Targets who succeed must mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}.

features.name: Crushing Grasp
features.text: When the Roc makes a successful standard attack, you can **mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to have the Roc crush the target with its talons, forcing them to mark **1d4** {{term:stress|Stress}} and _Restraining_ them until they succeed on a {{term:strength|Strength}} Roll (20).

features.name: Nest Warden
features.text: When the Roc’s eggs are threatened, it gains the following features:

features.name: Wrathful
features.text: The Roc gains a +2 bonus to its {{term:difficulty|Difficulty}} and a bonus to damage rolls equal to the number of {{term:stress|Stress}} it has marked.

features.name: Electrifying Aura
features.text: The Roc has {{term:resistance|resistance}} to magic damage. PCs who fail a roll within {{term:very-close|Very Close range}} must spend a {{term:hope|Hope}} or mark **1d4** {{term:stress|Stress}}.

name: Sandwyrm
text: _A gargantuan burrowing worm that has armor plating and gnashing_ _jaws. This intelligent and opportunistic hunter can swim through_ _sand as quickly as a cheetah runs on land._
motives: Ambush from below, eat and leave, tunnel and erupt, use both ends

features.name: Venomous Tail Stinger
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to attack a target within {{term:close|Close range}}. On a success, the target takes **3d10+2** physical damage and must succeed on a {{term:strength|Strength}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}} or become _{{term:restrained|Restrained}}_ and _{{term:vulnerable|Vulnerable}}_ until they roll with {{term:hope|Hope}}.

features.name: Devour
features.text: Make an attack against a target within {{term:melee|Melee range}}. On a success, the Sandwyrm _Swallows_ the target. While _Swallowed_, the target is _{{term:restrained|Restrained}}_ and marks a {{term:hit-points|HP}} when the Sandwyrm is spotlighted. The Sandwyrm disgorges all _Swallowed_ creatures when it takes Major or greater damage.

features.name: Hungry, Not Stupid
features.text: When the Sandwyrm marks half its {{term:hit-points|HP}} or _Swallows_ a creature, roll a **d6**. On a result of 3 or lower, the Sandwyrm retreats to safety.

name: Shapeshifting Fiend
text: _An evil entity who impersonates a trusted figure._
motives: Impersonate, sow discord, tempt betrayal

features.name: Fiendish Nature
features.text: The Fiend has {{term:resistance|resistance}} to magic damage and can’t be fooled by magic illusions.

features.name: Impersonate
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to have the Fiend magically transform into a humanoid they have previously interacted with. A PC who targets the Fiend while they’re in the form of a person the PC cares for must succeed on an {{term:instinct|Instinct}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}} or the attack fails and the PC must mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}.

features.name: Turn Invisible
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to make the Fiend _{{term:hidden|Hidden}}_ until they make an {{term:action-roll|action roll}} or take damage.

features.name: Backhanded Guidance
features.text: When a PC makes an {{term:action-roll|action roll}} while the Fiend is in the scene, you can **mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to add **1d6** to the result of their {{term:duality-dice|Fear Die}}.

features.name: Exposed! (Phase Change)
features.text: When the Fiend is defeated or the PCs discover its true identity, replace the Fiend with Shapeshifting Fiend Revealed and immediately {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} them.

name: Shapeshifting Fiend Revealed
text: _A towering humanoid who has an insectile head and multiple sets of_ _glowing red eyes._
motives: Claim souls, confuse and misdirect, escape to the Circles Below, teleport

features.name: Relentless (3)
features.text: The Fiend can be spotlighted up to three times per GM turn. Spend {{term:fear|Fear}} as usual to {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} them.

features.name: Fiendish Resistance
features.text: The Fiend has {{term:resistance|resistance}} to magic damage and can’t be fooled by magic illusions.

features.name: Demonic Rage
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to make a standard attack with a bonus to the attack roll equal the amount of {{term:stress|Stress}} the Fiend has marked. On a success, the attack deals {{term:direct-damage|direct damage}}.

features.name: Hall of Mirrors
features.text: **Mark 2 {{term:stress|Stress}}** to have the Fiend summon four illusory duplicates and activate a Duplicate Countdown (4). When the Fiend is targeted by an attack, they gain a bonus to their {{term:difficulty|Difficulty}} equal to the {{term:countdown|countdown}} die’s current value. The {{term:countdown|countdown}} ticks down when a PC fails an attack against the Fiend. When it triggers, the duplicates vanish.

features.name: Flash Claw
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to have the Fiend unleash an arc of magical energy. Make an attack roll against all targets within {{term:close|Close range}}. Targets the attack succeeds against take **3d20** magic damage.

features.name: Mind Games
features.text: When an attack targeting the Fiend from beyond {{term:very-close|Very Close range}} succeeds with {{term:fear|Fear}}, you can **mark a** **{{term:stress|Stress}}** to have the Fiend instantly switch places with a PC within {{term:very-close|Very Close range}}. The PC takes the damage instead.

name: Storm Titan
text: _An ancient, wise, and temperamental goliath who has hair made of_ _mist and electricity crackling across their skin._
motives: Erupt violently, wait, watch

features.name: Relentless (3)
features.text: The Titan can be spotlighted up to three times per GM turn. Spend {{term:fear|Fear}} as usual to {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} them.

features.name: Momentum
features.text: When the Titan makes a successful attack against a PC, you gain a {{term:fear|Fear}}.

features.name: Ball Lightning
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to have the Titan conjure **1d4** spheres of electrical energy within {{term:close|Close range}}. When the Titan is spotlighted, they can move each sphere up to {{term:close|Close range}}. When a sphere moves within {{term:very-close|Very Close range}} of a PC, the PC takes **4d6** magic damage, and the sphere disappears. Each sphere has the same {{term:difficulty|Difficulty}} as the Titan and disappears if a creature deals magic damage to it.

features.name: Storm Bringer
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to have the Titan conjure a raging storm. Each PC within {{term:close|Close range}} of the Titan must make a {{term:strength|Strength}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}}. Targets who fail take **3d12** magic damage and are _{{term:vulnerable|Vulnerable}}_ until they are spotlighted. Targets who succeed take half damage.

features.name: Thunderclap
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to target up to three PCs in front of the Titan within {{term:close|Close range}}. Each target marks a {{term:stress|Stress}} and becomes _{{term:vulnerable|Vulnerable}}_ until they roll with {{term:hope|Hope}}.

name: Stag Knight
text: _A knight with huge, majestic antlers wearing armor made of_ _dangerous thorns._
motives: Isolate, maneuver, protect the forest, weed the unwelcome

features.name: From Above
features.text: When the Knight succeeds on a standard attack from above a target, they deal **3d12+3** physical damage instead of their standard damage.

features.name: Blade of the Forest
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to make an attack against all targets within {{term:very-close|Very Close range}}. Targets the Knight succeeds against take physical damage equal to **3d4** + the target’s {{term:damage-thresholds|Major threshold}}.

features.name: Thorny Armor
features.text: When the Knight takes damage from an attack within {{term:melee|Melee range}}, you can **mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to deal **1d10+5** physical damage to the attacker.

name: Oak Treant
text: _A sturdy animate old-growth tree._
motives: Hide in plain sight, preserve the forest, root down, swing branches

features.name: Just a Tree
features.text: Before they make their first attack in a fight or after they become _{{term:hidden|Hidden}}_, the Treant is indistinguishable from other trees until they next act or a PC succeeds on an {{term:instinct|Instinct}} Roll to identify them.

features.name: Seed Barrage
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** and make an attack against up to three targets within {{term:close|Close range}}, pummeling them with giant acorns. Targets the Treant succeeds against take **2d10+5** physical damage.

features.name: Take Root
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to _Root_ the Treant in place. The Treant is _{{term:restrained|Restrained}}_ while _Rooted_, and can end this effect instead of moving while they are spotlighted. While Rooted, the Treant has {{term:resistance|resistance}} to physical damage.

name: Treant Sapling
text: _A small, sentient tree sapling._
motives: Blend in, preserve the forest, pummel, surround

features.name: Minion (6)
features.text: The Sapling is defeated when they take any damage. For every 6 damage a PC deals to the Sapling, defeat an additional Minion within range the attack would succeed against.

features.name: Group Attack
features.text: **Spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to choose a target and {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} all Treant Saplings within {{term:close|Close range}} of them. Those Minions move into {{term:melee|Melee range}} of the target and make one shared attack roll. On a success, they deal 8 physical damage each. Combine this damage.

name: Unicorn
text: _A celestial avatar of goodness in the form of a preternaturally_ _beautiful horse with a long, spiraled horn emerging from its head._
motives: Keep evil at bay, protect the sacred, sense emotions and intent

features.name: Celestial Lance
features.text: The Unicorn’s standard attack deals double damage to a creature that has dealt damage to it.

features.name: Healing Touch
features.text: The Unicorn touches its horn to an ally within {{term:melee|Melee range}} and channels healing energy into them. **Mark** **any number of {{term:stress|Stress}}** to clear an equal number of the ally’s {{term:hit-points|HP}}.

features.name: Protective Aura
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to have the Unicorn conjure a sparkling magical aura. While the aura is in effect, attack rolls made against the Unicorn or an ally within {{term:very-close|Very Close range}} are made with {{term:disadvantage|disadvantage}}. This effect lasts until the Unicorn takes damage.

features.name: Teleport
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to have the Unicorn teleport up to {{term:very-far|Very Far range}}. The Unicorn can bring up to three allies within {{term:very-close|Very Close range}} with it.

name: Head Vampire
text: _A captivating undead dressed in aristocratic finery._
motives: Create thralls, charm, command, fly, intimidate

features.name: Terrifying
features.text: When the Vampire makes a successful attack, all PCs within {{term:far|Far range}} lose a {{term:hope|Hope}} and you gain a {{term:fear|Fear}}.

features.name: Look into My Eyes
features.text: A creature who moves into {{term:melee|Melee range}} of the Vampire must make an {{term:instinct|Instinct}} {{term:reaction-roll|Reaction Roll}}. On a failure, you gain **1d4** {{term:fear|Fear}}.

features.name: Feed on Followers
features.text: When the Vampire is within {{term:melee|Melee range}} of an ally, they can cause the ally to mark a {{term:hit-points|HP}}. The Vampire then clears a {{term:hit-points|HP}}.

features.name: The Hunt Is On
features.text: **Spend 2 {{term:fear|Fear}}** to summon **1d4** Vampires, who appear at {{term:far|Far range}} and immediately take the {{term:spotlight|spotlight}}.

features.name: Lifesuck
features.text: When the Vampire is spotlighted, roll a **d8**. On a result of 6 or higher, all targets within {{term:very-close|Very Close range}} must mark a {{term:hit-points|HP}}.

name: Vampire Bat Swarm
text: _A cloud of blood-sucking bats._
motives: Blot out the moon, murmur, spread disease

features.name: Horde (2d6)
features.text: When the Swarm has marked half or more of its {{term:hit-points|HP}}, its standard attack deals **2d6** physical damage instead.

features.name: Blinding Multitude
features.text: The Swarm is so thick it blocks the vision of anyone it interacts with. Creatures within {{term:melee|Melee range}} have {{term:disadvantage|disadvantage}} on attacks made against adversaries other than the Swarm.

features.name: Bloodsuckers
features.text: When the Swarm deals damage to a target, you can **mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to have the Swarm feed. The target marks an additional {{term:hit-points|HP}}, and the Swarm clears a {{term:hit-points|HP}}.

name: Vampire
text: _An intelligent undead with blood-stained lips and a predator’s smile._
motives: Bite, charm, deceive, feed, intimidate

features.name: Draining Bite
features.text: Make an attack against a target within {{term:melee|Melee range}}. On a success, deal **5d4** physical damage. A target who marks {{term:hit-points|HP}} from this attack loses a {{term:hope|Hope}} and must mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}. The Vampire then clears a {{term:hit-points|HP}}.

features.name: Mistform
features.text: When the Vampire takes physical damage, you can **spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to take half damage.

name: Vampire Lord
text: _A cruel vampire lord from a long-lost age, cursed with immortality._
motives: Corrupt, destroy, overwhelm with evil power

features.name: Relentless (3)
features.text: The Vampire Lord can be spotlighted up to three times per GM turn. Spend {{term:fear|Fear}} as usual to {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} them.

features.name: Midnight Heart
features.text: _Long-Term Countdown (6)._ The Vampire Lord keeps their heart hidden in a safe place. If it’s destroyed, the Vampire Lord dies. Otherwise, when the Vampire Lord is defeated, activate the {{term:countdown|countdown}}. It ticks down each time the PCs finish a {{term:long-rest|long rest}}. When it triggers, the Vampire Lord revives within {{term:close|Close range}} of the heart with all {{term:hit-points|HP}} and {{term:stress|Stress}} cleared.

features.name: Terrifying
features.text: When the Vampire Lord makes a successful attack roll, all PCs within {{term:close|Close range}} lose a {{term:hope|Hope}}, and you gain a {{term:fear|Fear}}.

features.name: Unleash Hellfire
features.text: **Mark a {{term:stress|Stress}}** to have the Vampire Lord momentarily conjure **1d4** bursts of hellfire within {{term:far|Far range}}. Each burst deals **3d6** magic damage to each target within {{term:very-close|Very Close range}}. If a target takes damage from multiple bursts, combine the damage.

features.name: Resurgence
features.text: When a PC within {{term:very-close|Very Close range}} rolls with {{term:hope|Hope}}, you can **spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to clear a {{term:hit-points|HP}} or a {{term:stress|Stress}}.

features.name: Melt into Shadow
features.text: When a PC would deal damage to the Vampire Lord, you can **spend a {{term:fear|Fear}}** to roll a **d6**. On a result of 5 or higher, negate the damage, then teleport the Vampire Lord to a point within {{term:far|Far range}}.

features.name: Hellwing
features.text:
When the Vampire Lord marks half their {{term:hit-points|HP}}, they transform into the Hellwing: a towering, demonic bat creature. They gain the “On Crimson Wings” and “Bloodbath” features and replace their standard attack with the following standard attack:

**Claws:** Close | 3d12+6 phy

features.name: On Crimson Wings
features.text: While flying, the Hellwing gains a +1 bonus to their {{term:difficulty|Difficulty}}.

features.name: Bloodbath
features.text: When the Hellwing takes Major or greater damage, the ground within {{term:very-close|Very Close range}} is covered with blood, dealing **3d10** magic damage to all other creatures in the area. When the Hellwing takes the {{term:spotlight|spotlight}} on subsequent GM turns, all other creatures in that area take **3d6** magic damage.

name: Vault Guardian Gaoler
text: _A boxy, dust-covered construct with thick metallic swinging doors on_ _their torso._
motives: Carry away, entrap, protect, pummel

features.name: Blocking Shield
